notes: Briefs for the old-versus-new listening batch (experiments/listening_batch.py).
Every condition gets the same brief, the same controls, the same length and the same seed, so the pipeline is what differs.

Sung briefs use fixed lyrics so the words are held constant. Thodi's words come from the accepted recipe (r3); chai_bollywood uses the original Hindi fixture written for the earlier lyric research; the English ballad and the Hindi wedding song were written for this batch. None of them quote an existing song.

briefs.brief: Dawn on the Yamuna: an expressive bansuri leads over a tanpura drone and gentle tabla, sparse santoor, peaceful and luminous, no singing
A long slow evening raga on a rooftop, the sitar answering itself while the city goes quiet and the lamps come on, tabla joining later, no singing
Warm melodic piano hook answered by flute and acoustic guitar, strings swelling into a wordless choir chorus, hopeful
Epic cinematic orchestral piece, quiet strings at first, rising to a heroic climax with brass and big drums, no singing
A Hindi romantic acoustic ballad, warm male voice, fingerpicked guitar and piano, tender longing
A Bollywood romantic song about one more cup of tea at the window, strings and tabla, warm male voice
A festive Bollywood dance number for a wedding sangeet, dhol and synths, bright female voice, everyone dancing

briefs.brief: An English pop ballad on piano about the last train home after a breakup, quiet verses building to a big chorus with strings, female voice
briefs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Platform lights are flickering low
Your coat still smells of autumn rain
I count the stops I used to know
And trace your name across the pane

[Pre-Chorus]
And every station slips away
Like words I never learned to say

[Chorus]
On the last train home
I keep the seat beside me
On the last train home
Your shadow rides behind me

[Verse 2]
The window shows a stranger's face
Tired eyes and borrowed time
A ticket folded in its place
Your number underlined

[Bridge]
Maybe you're waiting at the end of the line
Maybe the lights are still on
Maybe I'm only counting the signs
Of a love that's already gone

[Chorus]
On the last train home
I keep the seat beside me
On the last train home
Your shadow rides behind me
